finding_groups.message: This is a true privacy/security-quality vulnerability, although not malicious code. Chrome Performance traces and genera
finding_groups.suggestion: This is a true privacy/security-quality vulnerability, although not malicious code. Chrome Performance traces and generated reports can contain sensitive or identifying information: internal URLs, script names, function names, stack/profile details, resource URLs, browser extension interference, user actions, host paths, and sometimes cookies or authentication-adjacent metadata depending on the trace and the application. The skill instructs decompression, analysis, report creation, and local Edge headless PDF generation, but does not warn the user about data sensitivity, artifact persistence, redaction before sharing, or the fact that it will execute local tools and browsers. That omission creates a realistic accidental data-leak or unsafe-execution surface. Additionally, the PDF step can load HTML into Edge headless; if Markdown-to-HTML output is not carefully sanitized, report content derived from trace data could trigger local HTML/JavaScript behavior or network fetches depending on renderer and platform settings. Add explicit security and privacy handling instructions. 1) At the top of SKILL.md, warn that trace files and generated reports may contain sensitive internal details and should be treated as confidential. 2) Require explicit user consent before decompressing a trace, writing intermediate files, generating reports, or launching Edge/Chrome headless. 3) Instruct the agent to avoid persisting raw decompressed traces unless necessary, and if necessary, write them to a temporary directory with a clear cleanup step. 4) Add a redaction/sanitization step before sharing or exporting: remove or replace user identifiers, URLs containing tokens, internal paths, environment-specific names, stack fragments, and sensitive script/function names when they are not essential to the report. 5) Generate PDF only from sanitized HTML, with HTML escaping enforced and raw HTML disabled or strictly allow-listed in md2html. 6) Prefer sandboxed or isolated PDF rendering; if local Edge is required, document that it runs locally, avoid --no-sandbox, and use flags or platform mechanisms that block background networking where supported, e.g. isolated temp user-data-dir, disabled extensions, and network restrictions if available. 7) Quote and validate file paths used in commands; reject traversal or shell metacharacters in user-supplied filenames. Suggested warning block: 'Security note: Performance traces can reveal internal application structure, URLs, scripts, functions, and user-related behavior. Decompressed traces and reports may persist sensitive data. Do not share raw traces or unredacted reports. The analysis may write files and launch a local headless browser for PDF output. Use a controlled environment, redact sensitive details, and clean up artifacts before sharing.'

metadata.llm_reasoning: Chrome traces and generated reports can contain sensitive URLs, paths, identifiers, and internal application details; the skill instructs decompression, file writes, and headless Edge PDF generation without privacy/redaction guidance, and md2html link handling can emit unsafe hrefs.

Add explicit security and privacy handling instructions. 1) At the top of SKILL.md, warn that trace files and generated reports may contain sensitive internal details and should be treated as confidential. 2) Require explicit user consent before decompressing a trace, writing intermediate files, generating reports, or launching Edge/Chrome headless. 3) Instruct the agent to avoid persisting raw decompressed traces unless necessary, and if necessary, write them to a temporary directory with a clear cleanup step. 4) Add a redaction/sanitization step before sharing or exporting: remove or replace user identifiers, URLs containing tokens, internal paths, environment-specific names, stack fragments, and sensitive script/function names when they are not essential to the report. 5) Generate PDF only from sanitized HTML, with HTML escaping enforced and raw HTML disabled or strictly allow-listed in md2html. 6) Prefer sandboxed or isolated PDF rendering; if local Edge is required, document that it runs locally, avoid --no-sandbox, and use flags or platform mechanisms that block background networking where supported, e.g. isolated temp user-data-dir, disabled extensions, and network restrictions if available. 7) Quote and validate file paths used in commands; reject traversal or shell metacharacters in user-supplied filenames. Suggested warning block: 'Security note: Performance traces can reveal internal application structure, URLs, scripts, functions, and user-related behavior. Decompressed traces and reports may persist sensitive data. Do not share raw traces or unredacted reports. The analysis may write files and launch a local headless browser for PDF output. Use a controlled environment, redact sensitive details, and clean up artifacts before sharing.'
